consolidation.summary:
BLOCK on one clause, in two files. Six of seven items pass; r3-evidence fails.

The gate's own question was "is the vocabulary TRUE?", and two of its three factual claims are true and now measured independently, in fresh processes with explicit paths as ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT s.Dogfooding requires: (a) with your own lease held, spine_bind to a second checklist is REFUSED with the exact text the specs quote, and a positive control proves the refusal is scoped to precisely that condition -- the identical call SUCCEEDS once the lease is released; (b) a role dispatched with no spine of its own binds and drives one through the door, identity derived from the spine's own work id, which this survey is itself a live instance of. So the vocabulary neither promises a path that does not exist nor strands a role without one.

The third claim does not survive. Both files state that "the archive gate requires the lease to cover every journaled action, so releasing it to reach a second checklist fails your own closeout". The archive gate is a Commander-spine gate whose only lease-related postcondition is c3 "engine session lease released" with check=null; spine_lifecycle.close_work refuses in the opposite direction (while the lease is still ACTIVE); the real lease-window enforcement lives in evals/euler-*/checks/spine_completed.py::journal_consistent and runs only under the eval harness; and neither crew plan has a closeout gate at all. The inherited SKILL.md wording the implementer paraphrased -- "the terminal provenance check" -- was accurate; "archive gate" appears nowhere in skills/. The IMPLEMENTER_RESULT offers no measurement for this clause.

This is worth a BLOCK rather than an override because of where it sits: inside a sentence that advertises itself as "a measured refusal rather than an oversight", in the two files this change makes the corpus's statement of what the door is for a role. The handoff is explicit that the REASON exists so a future author cannot "fix" the rule; a future author who checks this reason finds no archive gate in their own plan and is entitled to discount the whole paragraph. The remedy is one clause in two files -- quote the inherited "terminal provenance check" wording instead of renaming it -- and the Fowler pass flags that the paragraph is duplicated near-verbatim, so the repair must land in both.

Everything else holds and was re-run, not trusted: TOML parses (exit 0); the guard reports no specs/ address, and its silence there is non-vacuous by census, by all five walk floors passing, and by a positive control that injected a CLI clause into an in-memory copy of the same guarded text and watched both patterns fire; the schema decision (prose only, no new keys) is correct, re-derived from _compile_gate's fixed field list, and confirmed by compiling both specs and observing the comment dropped while the prose survives; the config_ref record is accurate at every leg and leaving it was right. Three triage candidates flagged, one of which (tc3) should reach the Admiral before g5-final locks the sweep wording: notes-1.md s.M1's "the door provably cannot / the CLI is the only path" holds only for a process already holding a lease, not for the dispatched-crew case it was mostly about.

triage_candidates.statement: "The lease must cover every journaled action" is stated as binding doctrine in skills/reviewer/SKILL.md:17 and skills/implementer/SKILL.md:17, but its only enforcement is evals/euler-*/checks/spine_completed.py::journal_consistent, which runs from that file's own main() over an eval RUN DIRECTORY. No production path enforces it: not the Commander archive gate (postcondition c3 is "engine session lease released", check=null), not spine_lifecycle.close_work (which refuses only while the lease is still ACTIVE), not checklist_engine, not run_crew.py, not verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py. So every crew is told a rule that holds only under the eval harness. Either the rule should be enforced on a real run or the doctrine should say where it bites. Out of scope for g3 (skills/** is fenced from this lane) and it is the upstream cause of the g3 BLOCK finding, so fixing the specs' clause does not close this.

The dangling config_ref contradiction is wider than specs/ and the existing candidate (.agent-work/567-d1/triage-candidates/engine-config-json-absent.md) scopes it to the two spec files only. skills/reviewer/templates/REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json and its .agent-work/templates/ overlay copy -- the file a reviewer actually instantiates from, and the one this survey was built from -- carry the same config_ref = "docs/agents/engine-config.json" while being type=survey, against the pinned CYCLE.template.json precedent (tests/test_explorer_templates.py:242-247: a survey never consults rework_cap, so the key is dropped rather than pointed at a file a fresh install won't have). Whoever settles the survey half must sweep the templates, not just specs/reviewer.spine.toml, or the two halves drift again.

FLOAT TO THE ADMIRAL BEFORE g5-final LOCKS THE SWEEP WORDING. .agent-work/567-d1/notes-1.md s.M1 concluded the door "provably cannot" reach the three second-checklist sites and that the CLI is "the only path" for them. Measured independently in this review (fresh process, door_probe.py case unbound-then-bind) and true of this survey itself: a crew dispatched with no SPINE_FILE holds no lease, binds its own plan or survey through spine_bind, and drives it entirely through the door -- identity derived from the spine's own work_id, never supplied.
